texto: In Italian the double consonants (**doppie**) are pronounced with greater tension and duration than the simple ones: **penna** (pen) does not sound the same as **pena** (pity, pity); **notte** (night) does not sound the same as **note** (notes). The difference is phonological and distinguishes meanings.

In Italian, mandatory tylde is written in the acute words polysyllic that end in vocal: **città**, **perché**, **caffè**, **lunedì**, **università**. Also in some monosyls to avoid confusion: **è** (en / esta, of the verb * essere *) versus **e** (conjunction * and *); **sì** (affirmation) against **si** (pronoun).

frases.it: Buongiorno! Ha una penna blu, per favore?
frases.es: ¡Buenos días! ¿Tiene un bolígrafo azul, por favor?
frases.en: Good morning! Do you have a blue pen, please?

frases.it: Sì, certo! Ecco qui la penna. Serve altro?
frases.es: ¡Sí, claro! Aquí tiene el bolígrafo. ¿Le hace falta algo más?
frases.en: Yeah, right! Here's the pen. Do you need anything else?

frases.es: Sí, un cuaderno para la universidad.

frases.it: Oggi è lunedì, c'è lo sconto su tutto!
frases.es: Hoy es lunes, ¡hay descuento en todo!
frases.en: Today is Monday, there's a discount on everything!

frases.es: ¡Perfecto, muchas gracias! ¡Que tenga un buen día!
frases.en: Perfect, thank you very much! Have a good day!

bloques.pregunta: Why is it essential to pronounce the double consonants in Italian well?

opciones.texto: Because holding the consonant longer can change the meaning of the word.
opciones.explicacion: For example, «penna» (pen) and «pena» (penalty) are different words.

opciones.texto: Because double consonants always indicate that the word is plural.
opciones.explicacion: They are not related to the morphological plural.

opciones.texto: Because a double consonant is always typed.
opciones.explicacion: The double consonants do not add any tilde.

bloques.pregunta: In what cases is it mandatory to write a graphic accent in Italian?

opciones.texto: In polysyllic words with an accent on the last syllable, such as «città», «caffè» or «lunedì».
opciones.explicacion: The sharp words of more than one syllable always carry tylde written in the final vowel.

opciones.texto: In all the plain words or drújulas.
opciones.explicacion: In Italian, it is not marked in plain words or regular slate.
The graphic accent is orthographic and lexic, not entonative.

bloques.frase: Carlos ha comprato una ___ per scrivere.

opciones.explicacion: «Penna» with double «n» means pen or pen.
«Pena» with a single «n» means suffering or pity.
There is no such word in this context.
«Oggi» = today; «è» = es; «lunedì» = Monday (with mandatory end tilde).
«Oggi è lunedì» claims today is Monday.

bloques.frase: La tazza di ___ è sul tavolo.

opciones.explicacion: «Caffè» has a mandatory graphic accent on the final «è».
Without accent it is not the correct orthographic writing in Italian.
Italian writing is double «ff» and typed in the «è».

bloques.pregunta: What is the difference between «è» and «e»?

opciones.texto: «È» with accent is the verb being / being; «e» without accent is the conjunction «and».
opciones.explicacion: The graphic accent distinguishes these two homophone words.

opciones.texto: «È» is a preposition and «e» is a pronoun.
There's no difference, they can be freely exchanged.
opciones.explicacion: The presence or absence of tilde completely changes the grammatical function.

intro: The double consonants are pronounced with longer duration and can change the meaning; the words are called "acute" with a mandatory written accent.
